learning_outcomes.description: Understand professional legal practice through engaging directly in legally-oriented work.
Understand and critically appreciate the role and value of lawyering in the context of the organisation where the internship is completed.
Understand the practice dimensions of the particular legal area relevant to the internship.
Have greater insight into their own learning and professional identity.
Bring critical insight into some of the challenges and opportunities facing lawyers and/or organisations and the social, financial, and legal frameworks within which they operate.
A deeper understanding of, and increased capacity to engage with, law, policy and reform in the area of the internship.

assessments.assessment_title: Attendance at Placement (120 hours) AND Attendance at 2 x Teaching Workshops
assessments.task_description: Attendance is an inherent requirement of this course. Students are expected to attend their placement for a total of 120 hours throughout the semester, including any induction or debriefing sessions required by their supervising organisation. Attendance will be verified with supervising organisations. Students are also required to attend and participate in two (2) x 2 hour in-person teaching workshops held throughout semester. These workshops will be held in the second and last weeks of semester - exact time and location TBC (Details will be provided on Blackboard).
assessments.submission_guidelines: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.

assessments.task_description: Students are required to complete a Student Learning Plan which provides details of their placement arrangements, an overview of relevant tasks and activities they anticipate being involved with during the placement, and a brief reflection on their learning goals for the semester arising from the placement opportunity. A template will be provided on Blackboard for students to complete and this can also be used as a basis for discussion with placement supervisors, as appropriate.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Learning Plans must be submitted electronically via the submission link on the course Blackboard site.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description: Students are required to submit a reflective journal covering a range of topics, including an assessment of the placement experience against their original learning plan, a reflection on activities/insights gained from each of the teaching workshops, and a thoughtful review of how the placement experience developed their understanding of professional practice and their own career goals and development. A detailed task sheet with prompt questions will be available to students on the Blackboard site to guide reflective responses. They should also prepare a 5 min talk about their placement experience, drawing on their reflective journal, which will be presented during the workshop in the final week of semester.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Reflective Journals must be submitted electronically via the submission link on the course Blackboard site.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.
